items.s: If it ___ tomorrow, we will hold the fair indoors.
items.h: First conditional: if + present, then will: If it rains, we will...

items.s: If I ___ you, I would check my answers again.
items.h: For advice, use the past form were: If I were you, I would...

items.s: If we had left earlier, we ___ caught the train.
items.h: Third conditional: if + had done, then would have done.

items.s: If she ___ the bus, she would have been late.
items.h: Third conditional: if + had + past participle: if she had missed...

items.s: If you heat ice above zero degrees, it ___.
items.h: Facts take the present in both parts: if you heat ice, it melts.

items.s: Unless we ___ the plants, they will dry out.
items.h: After unless, use the present for the future: unless we water...

items.s: I would buy a telescope if I ___ enough money.
items.h: Second conditional: would + verb, and if + past: if I had...

items.s: If the robot ___ charged, it wouldn't have stopped.
items.h: Past unreal: if it had been charged, it wouldn't have stopped.

items.s: If I ___ about the quiz yesterday, I'd have revised.
items.h: Past regret: if + had + past participle: if I had known...

items.s: If we planted more trees, the air ___ cleaner.
items.h: If + past, then would + verb: the air would be cleaner.

items.s: What ___ you do if you found a dinosaur egg?
items.h: Imagining something? Use would + verb, with if + past.

items.s: I wish I ___ my umbrella this morning!
items.h: A wish about the past takes had + past participle: I wish I had...

items.s: The Mona Lisa ___ by Leonardo da Vinci.
items.h: Passive past: was + past participle, with the doer after by.

items.s: English ___ in many countries around the world.
items.h: Passive present: is + past participle: English is spoken.

items.s: The new bridge over the river will ___ next summer.
items.h: Future passive: will be + past participle: it will be built.

items.s: Our class project has ___ chosen for the science fair!
items.h: Present perfect passive: has been + past participle: has been chosen.

items.s: The pyramids ___ built thousands of years ago.
items.h: Plural subject, past passive: the pyramids were built.

items.s: The match was ___ because of the heavy rain.
items.h: Passive: was + past participle. British spelling: cancelled, double l.

items.s: Penicillin ___ discovered by accident in 1928.
items.h: A finished past date needs the past passive: was discovered.

items.s: The hall ___ decorated before the guests arrived.
items.h: Done before another past event: had been + past participle.

items.s: Your essay must ___ in by Friday.
items.h: After must, the passive is be + past participle: be handed in.

items.s: I have ___ for the bus for twenty minutes!
items.h: Still going on now: have been + -ing: I have been waiting.

items.s: She has been ___ the violin since she was six.
items.h: Use has been + -ing for an action going on since a past time.

items.s: How long have you ___ learning French?
items.h: Present perfect continuous: have + been + -ing.

items.s: Your hands are covered in paint. ___ you been painting?
items.h: Have you been + -ing? asks about a recent activity.

items.s: It ___ raining since early this morning.
items.h: With since, use has been + -ing: it has been raining since...

items.s: When we arrived, the film ___ already started.
items.h: The earlier of two past events takes had: it had already started.

items.s: By the time I got there, everyone ___ home.
items.h: By the time + past: the earlier event takes had + past participle.

items.s: She ___ seen snow before she visited Norway.
items.h: Before a past event, use had: she had never seen snow before...

items.s: After he ___ his homework, he went outside to play.
items.h: The first of two past actions can take had: after he had finished.

items.s: I suddenly realised I ___ my keys at school.
items.h: Something done even earlier in the past takes had: I had left them.

items.s: Ella said that she ___ excited about the school trip.
items.h: Reported speech often moves back a tense: 'I am' becomes she was.

items.s: He told us he ___ the race the day before.
items.h: Reported past news moves back: 'I won' becomes he had won.

items.s: Dad promised that he ___ take us to the zoo.
items.h: In reported speech, will becomes would: he said he would...

items.s: The teacher told us ___ quiet during the test.
items.h: Reported orders use tell + person + to: she told us to be quiet.

items.s: My grandad really enjoys ___ in the sea.
items.h: Enjoy is followed by -ing: he enjoys swimming.

items.s: We decided ___ a robot for the science fair.
items.h: Decide is followed by to + verb: we decided to build.

items.s: Would you mind ___ the window, please?
items.h: Mind is followed by -ing: Would you mind opening...?

items.s: She hopes ___ an astronaut one day.
items.h: Hope is followed by to + verb: she hopes to become.

items.s: He finally gave up ___ to fix the old radio.
items.h: Give up is followed by -ing: he gave up trying.

items.s: I'm looking forward to ___ my pen pal in July.
items.h: Here to is a preposition, so add -ing: looking forward to meeting.

items.s: Remember ___ the lights off when you leave.
items.h: Remember to do something = don't forget to do it.

items.s: I'll never forget ___ the Northern Lights last winter.
items.h: Forget + -ing is about a memory: I'll never forget seeing...

items.s: Stop ___ and listen to the instructions, please!
items.h: Stop + -ing means end an activity: stop talking.

items.s: Our class is considering ___ a school garden.
items.h: Consider is followed by -ing: we are considering starting.

items.s: She managed ___ the puzzle in under a minute.
items.h: Manage is followed by to + verb: she managed to solve it.

items.s: Are you interested in ___ the chess club?
items.h: After a preposition like in, use -ing: interested in joining.

items.s: My parents let me ___ up late on Fridays.
items.h: Let + person + verb with no to: they let me stay up.

items.s: The funny ending made the whole audience ___.
items.h: Make + person + verb without to: it made everyone laugh.

items.s: We ___ in this town since 2019.
items.h: Since + a starting point needs the present perfect: have lived.

items.s: I used to ___ broccoli, but now I love it.
items.h: Used to + verb describes a past habit or state: I used to hate it.

items.s: She is used to ___ up early for swimming training.
items.h: Be used to (= be familiar with) is followed by -ing: getting up.

items.s: This time tomorrow, we will be ___ over the Atlantic.
items.h: Future continuous: will be + -ing for an action in progress.

items.s: By the end of the year, we will ___ read ten books.
items.h: Future perfect: will have + past participle = done by then.

items.s: While I ___ my bike, I saw a deer in the woods.
items.h: A longer action in progress in the past: was + -ing.

items.s: The explorers ___ shelter in a cave during the storm.
items.h: Seek is irregular: seek, sought, sought (like think, thought).

items.s: The sun ___ brightly all afternoon at the beach.
items.h: Shine is irregular: shine, shone, shone.

items.s: My woolly jumper ___ in the hot wash last week.
items.h: Shrink is irregular: shrink, shrank, shrunk.

items.s: She ___ me her book about volcanoes last week.
items.h: Lend, lent, lent. You lend to someone and borrow from someone.

items.s: The cyclist ___ three riders on the last hill yesterday.
items.h: Overtake works like take: take, took, so overtake, overtook.

items.s: The ice skater ___ round and round on the spot.
items.h: Spin is irregular: spin, spun, spun.

items.s: I forgot my coat, and now I'm cold. I ___ have brought it.
items.h: Should have + past participle = a good idea that you didn't do.

items.s: The ground is wet. It ___ have rained in the night.
items.h: Sure about the past from evidence? Use must have: it must have rained.

items.s: Mia ___ have eaten the cake. She was with me all day!
items.h: Sure something didn't happen? Use can't have: she can't have.

items.s: We ___ have hurried; the film started late.
items.h: Needn't have = you did it, but it wasn't necessary.

items.s: When I was five, I ___ swim, but now I can.
items.h: Past ability uses could: I couldn't swim then, but I can now.

items.s: You ___ touch the oven; it's very hot!
items.h: Mustn't = not allowed or dangerous. Needn't = not necessary.

items.s: On trip days you ___ to wear uniform; it's optional.
items.h: Don't have to = it isn't necessary. Mustn't = it isn't allowed.

items.s: ___ I borrow your pencil, please?
items.h: Ask politely for permission with may: May I borrow...?

items.s: You ___ better hurry, or you'll miss the bus.
items.h: Had better = strong advice: you had better hurry.

items.s: It's cloudy, so it ___ rain. Take a coat just in case.
items.h: Might = maybe: it might rain, so take a coat just in case.

items.s: With a bit more practice, we ___ have won the cup.
items.h: Could have + past participle = it was possible, but it didn't happen.

items.s: You ___ to eat more vegetables; they are good for you.
items.h: Ought is followed by to: you ought to eat more vegetables.

items.s: It's six, and Grandma said six, so that ___ be her.
items.h: Must = I'm sure it's true: that must be Grandma.

items.s: ___ I help you carry those heavy bags?
items.h: Offer help with Shall I...? Shall I help you carry them?

items.s: Students ___ not use calculators; it's against the rules.
items.h: May not = not allowed (formal): you may not use calculators.

items.s: I'd ___ stay in and read than go to the cinema.
items.h: Would rather + verb + than: I'd rather read than go out.

items.s: We ___ to leave now if we want to catch the train.
items.h: Need to + verb = it's necessary: we need to leave now.

items.s: Will you ___ to come to my party on Saturday?
items.h: Can has no future form, so use will be able to.

items.s: The boy ___ dog won the prize is in my class.
items.h: Whose shows belonging: the boy whose dog won the prize.

items.s: This is the museum ___ we saw the dinosaur bones.
items.h: For a place followed by a full clause, use where: the museum where...

items.s: Mount Everest, ___ is in Asia, is the world's highest peak.
items.h: After a comma, use which (not that) for things: Everest, which...

items.s: My aunt, ___ lives in Wales, is a vet.
items.h: After a comma, use who (not that) for people: my aunt, who...

items.s: The scientist to ___ we spoke was very helpful.
items.h: After a preposition, use whom for people: to whom we spoke.

items.s: That's the day ___ we first met our new teacher.
items.h: For a time followed by a full clause, use when: the day when...

items.s: The robot can switch ___ off when it gets too hot.
items.h: When the doer acts on itself, use a reflexive: itself.

items.s: The two pen pals write to ___ every week.
items.h: Two people doing it to one another: they write to each other.

items.s: Help ___ to some biscuits, everyone!
items.h: Talking to a group? The reflexive is yourselves (with -ves).

items.s: ___ of the two answers is correct?
items.h: Use which to choose from a small set: which of the two?

items.s: The prize goes to ___ finishes the puzzle first.
items.h: Whoever = any person who: the prize goes to whoever finishes first.

items.s: Is this pencil case ___ or mine?
items.h: Possessive pronouns have no apostrophe: yours, hers, ours.

items.s: The book, ___ cover is torn, belongs to the library.
items.h: Whose works for things too: the book, whose cover is torn...

items.s: My sister and ___ built a robot together.
items.h: Take away 'my sister and': I built it, so my sister and I built it.

items.s: The coach gave Sam and ___ a medal.
items.h: After a verb, use me: gave me a medal, so gave Sam and me.

items.s: Tell me the reason ___ you were late.
items.h: After the reason, use why: the reason why you were late.

items.s: I have two brothers, both of ___ love football.
items.h: After of, use whom for people: both of whom love football.

items.s: The children made the costumes all by ___.
items.h: All by themselves = with no help. The plural reflexive is themselves.

items.s: Everyone in the class ___ finished the test.
items.h: Everyone is singular, so it takes has: everyone has finished.

items.s: Physics ___ my favourite subject this year.
items.h: Physics looks plural, but it is one subject: physics is.

items.s: The news ___ very good today!
items.h: News is uncountable and takes a singular verb: the news is good.

items.s: One of my friends ___ a pet tortoise.
items.h: One of... takes a singular verb: one of my friends has.

items.s: There ___ a lot of people at the concert last night.
items.h: A lot of people is plural, and last night is past: there were.

items.s: The number of students in the club ___ grown this year.
items.h: The number of... is singular: the number has grown.

items.s: Rainbows and eclipses are natural ___.
items.h: Phenomenon comes from Greek: one phenomenon, two phenomena.

items.s: The judges used three ___ to choose the winner.
items.h: One criterion, two criteria: the -on ending becomes -a.

items.s: Scientists found three new ___ growing on the log.
items.h: Fungus comes from Latin: one fungus, two fungi.

items.s: The desert has two ___ where travellers can find water.
items.h: Words ending in -is change to -es: one oasis, two oases.

items.s: Caterpillars are the ___ of butterflies and moths.
items.h: One larva, two larvae: the -a ending becomes -ae.

items.s: Scientists discovered two new ___ of frog.
items.h: Species is the same in the singular and the plural.

items.s: Three ___ flew over the stadium during the show.
items.h: Aircraft stays the same in the plural: three aircraft.

items.s: She wants to study at ___ university in Scotland.
items.h: University starts with a 'you' sound, so use a: a university.

items.s: It took us ___ hour to walk to the top of the hill.
items.h: The h in hour is silent, so it starts with a vowel sound: an hour.

items.s: ___ Amazon is the largest rainforest on Earth.
items.h: Famous rivers, oceans and rainforests take the: the Amazon.

items.s: The Nile is one of ___ longest rivers in the world.
items.h: Superlatives take the: one of the longest, the biggest, the best.

items.s: Can I have ___ advice about my science project?
items.h: Advice is uncountable: some advice, never an advice.

items.s: We didn't have ___ homework last night.
items.h: Homework is uncountable; in negatives use any: not any homework.

items.s: It's ___ to swim across the Atlantic Ocean.
items.h: Possible takes the prefix im-: impossible (not unpossible).

items.s: Leaving your bike unlocked is very ___.
items.h: -less means without: careless = without enough care.

items.s: There has been a huge ___ in robot technology.
items.h: -ment turns a verb into a noun: develop becomes development.

items.s: She answered every question ___ and got full marks.
items.h: To say how she answered, use an adverb with -ly: correctly.

items.s: The ___ of the wheel changed transport forever.
items.h: -ion turns a verb into a noun: invent becomes invention.

items.s: Thank you for your ___; you made my day!
items.h: -ness turns an adjective into a noun: kind becomes kindness.

items.s: The map was so ___ that we found the castle easily.
items.h: -ful means full of: a useful map helps; a useless one doesn't.

items.s: I ___ with you; I think cats are better than dogs.
items.h: The opposite of agree takes the prefix dis-: disagree.

items.s: Don't ___ the instructions, or the model won't work.
items.h: The prefix mis- means wrongly: misread = read wrongly.

items.s: My tablet is flat, so I need to ___ it.
items.h: The prefix re- means again: recharge = charge again.

items.s: The magician made the coin ___.
items.h: The opposite of appear takes dis-: disappear.

items.s: His handwriting is so ___ that nobody can read it.
items.h: Before l, in- becomes il-: illegible, illegal, illogical.

items.s: Go is an ___ verb: go, went, gone.
items.h: Before r, in- becomes ir-: irregular, irresponsible.

items.s: The average ___ of the ocean is about 3,700 metres.
items.h: The noun from deep is depth (like wide, width and long, length).

items.s: Everyone was ___ by the size of the dinosaur skeleton.
items.h: -ed describes how you feel; -ing describes what causes it.

items.s: The documentary about sharks was really ___.
items.h: The thing that interests you is -ing: a fascinating documentary.

items.s: Our teacher gave us a clear ___ of the experiment.
items.h: The noun from explain is explanation (no i after the first a).

items.s: The weightlifter showed great ___ in the final.
items.h: The noun from strong is strength: she showed great strength.

items.s: My little brother is very ___; he never sits still.
items.h: To describe a person, use an adjective: energy becomes energetic.

items.s: We were ___ that the sun would come out.
items.h: Hopeful = full of hope; hopeless = without hope.

items.s: The scientist made an important ___.
items.h: After an important, we need a noun: discover becomes discovery.

items.s: Please speak ___; the baby is asleep.
items.h: To say how someone speaks, use an adverb: speak quietly.

items.s: It was very ___ of you to share your lunch.
items.h: It was + adjective + of you: generous. Generosity is the noun.

items.s: Someone who plays the piano is a ___.
items.h: -ist means a person who does it: piano becomes pianist.

items.s: The museum's ___ collection is worth millions.
items.h: -able makes an adjective: value becomes valuable (drop the e).

items.s: The robot moved with amazing ___.
items.h: After amazing, we need a noun: accurate becomes accuracy.

items.s: Unlike the ancient castle, the library is very ___.
items.h: Unlike signals a contrast: the opposite of ancient is modern.

items.s: Some animals are rare, but pigeons are very ___.
items.h: But signals a contrast: the opposite of rare is common.

items.s: Gold is valuable, but this plastic ring is ___.
items.h: Careful! Priceless means very valuable; worthless means no value.

items.s: The first question was simple, but the second was ___.
items.h: But signals a contrast: the opposite of simple is complicated.

items.s: Fairy tales are fiction, but this atlas is ___.
items.h: Non- means not: non-fiction books are full of true facts.

items.s: The rabbit is timid, but the lion is ___.
items.h: But signals a contrast: the opposite of timid is brave.

items.s: Magnets can attract each other, or they can ___ each other.
items.h: Attract means pull together; repel means push apart.

items.s: The more you practise, the ___ you will get.
items.h: The more..., the better...: both parts use comparatives.

items.s: Jupiter is ___ larger than Earth.
items.h: To make a comparative stronger, use much or far: much larger.

items.s: This puzzle is not as difficult ___ the last one.
items.h: As ... as compares two things: not as difficult as the last one.

items.s: There are ___ cars on the road on Sundays than on Mondays.
items.h: Use fewer for things you can count: fewer cars, less traffic.

items.s: Mercury is the ___ planet to the Sun.
items.h: Short adjectives add -est for superlatives: close, closest.

items.s: This is the ___ interesting book I have ever read.
items.h: Long adjectives use most for superlatives: the most interesting.

items.s: Cheetahs run ___ than any other land animal.
items.h: Than any other needs a comparative: faster than any other.

items.s: This is by ___ the best project in the class.
items.h: By far makes a superlative stronger: by far the best.

items.s: Is a blue whale ___ than an elephant?
items.h: Heavy ends in a consonant + y, so it becomes heavier.

items.s: ___ it was raining, we still enjoyed the picnic.
items.h: Although links two contrasting ideas: although it rained, we...

items.s: ___ the cold weather, the team trained outside.
items.h: Despite is followed by a noun, not a clause: despite the weather.

items.s: Pack an umbrella ___ it rains on the way home.
items.h: In case = to be ready if something happens: in case it rains.

items.s: You won't get better at chess ___ you practise.
items.h: Unless means if not: you won't improve unless you practise.

items.s: I saved my pocket money ___ I could buy a telescope.
items.h: So that shows purpose: I saved so that I could buy it.

items.s: Lily loves maths, ___ her brother prefers art.
items.h: Whereas compares two different things: she likes maths, whereas he...

items.s: ___ we finish our project, we can play outside.
items.h: Once = as soon as: once we finish, we can play.

items.s: She stayed calm, ___ the test was very hard.
items.h: Even though shows a surprising contrast, like a strong although.

items.s: The museum was closed. ___, the park was open.
items.h: However starts a new sentence to show a contrast, then a comma.

items.s: He asked ___ I wanted to join the club.
items.h: Reported yes/no questions use if or whether: he asked if I wanted...

items.s: ___ I was walking home, I saw a shooting star.
items.h: While goes with a clause; during goes with a noun: during the walk.

items.s: I was very tired; ___, I went to bed early.
items.h: Therefore means so; it introduces a result.

items.s: You can borrow my bike ___ you bring it back by six.
items.h: Provided = only if: you can borrow it provided you return it.

items.s: Neither Tom ___ Sara could solve the riddle.
items.h: Neither goes with nor: neither Tom nor Sara.

items.s: Not only is it fast, ___ it is also safe.
items.h: Not only ... but also: not only fast, but also safe.

items.s: Paw prints were ___ that the cat had stolen the fish.
items.h: Evidence = facts or signs that show something is true.

items.s: We made an ___ of how many sweets were in the jar.
items.h: An estimate is a careful guess: an estimate of how many.

items.s: Scientists ___ the data to find patterns.
items.h: Analyse = study something closely to understand it (British -yse).

items.s: A ___ is an idea that scientists test with an experiment.
items.h: A hypothesis is an idea you test; a conclusion comes afterwards.

items.s: There was a ___ improvement in her reading; it was huge.
items.h: Significant = large or important enough to notice.

items.s: Dinosaurs became ___ about 66 million years ago.
items.h: Extinct = no longer living anywhere on Earth.

items.s: Many birds ___ to warmer countries every autumn.
items.h: Migrate = travel to another place for a season, as birds do.

items.s: The Moon takes about 27 days to ___ the Earth.
items.h: Orbit = travel round a planet or star: the Moon orbits the Earth.

items.s: A polar bear's natural ___ is the Arctic.
items.h: A habitat is the natural home of an animal or plant.

items.s: This bag is ___; you can see everything inside it.
items.h: Transparent = see-through. Opaque = you can't see through it.

items.s: The art exhibition is ___; it closes next week.
items.h: Temporary = lasting a short time. Permanent = lasting for ever.

items.s: Please ___ the two maps and spot the differences.
items.h: Compare = look at things together to see how they differ.

items.s: We ___ the plants every day and wrote down what we saw.
items.h: Observe = watch carefully, the way a scientist does.

items.s: Water, food and sleep are ___ for good health.
items.h: Essential = absolutely necessary.

items.s: The weather forecast ___ sunshine for tomorrow.
items.h: Predict = say what will happen in the future.

items.s: Everyone can ___ to the class project by sharing an idea.
items.h: Contribute = give something, like ideas or help, to a shared goal.

items.s: This ___ engine does its job well and wastes no energy.
items.h: Efficient = doing a job well without wasting energy.

items.s: The ___ of the experiment was that plants need light.
items.h: A conclusion is what you decide at the end, from the results.

items.s: We did a ___ to find out pupils' favourite fruit.
items.h: A survey asks many people the same questions.

items.s: It was ___ that he was happy; he couldn't stop smiling.
items.h: Obvious = easy to see or understand.

items.s: Turning off lights helps us ___ energy.
items.h: Conserve = save something so it isn't wasted or lost.

items.s: Electric cars produce fewer harmful ___ than petrol cars.
items.h: Emissions are gases sent into the air, like car exhaust.

items.s: Our town has a ___ of about 50,000 people.
items.h: Population = the number of people living in a place.

items.s: The ___ of our trip is to learn about rivers.
items.h: Purpose = the reason for doing something. A porpoise is a sea animal!

items.s: This ancient vase is very ___; please handle it with care.
items.h: Fragile = easily broken, so handle it gently.

items.s: The loud music didn't ___ my concentration at all.
items.h: Affect is usually the verb; effect is usually the noun.

items.s: Music has a calming ___ on our dog.
items.h: After a or an, use the noun effect: a calming effect.

items.s: My coach gave me some useful ___ before the race.
items.h: Advice (with c) is the noun; advise (with s) is the verb.

items.s: I would ___ you to take a map with you.
items.h: Advise (with s) is the verb: I advise you. Advice is the noun.

items.s: I need to ___ the piano every day before the concert.
items.h: In British English, practise (with s) is the verb, practice the noun.

items.s: Football ___ is on Tuesdays after school.
items.h: Practice (with c) is the noun: football practice.

items.s: The college ___ gave a speech at the prize-giving.
items.h: Principal = the person in charge; principle = a rule or belief.

items.s: Honesty is an important ___ to live by.
items.h: A principle is a rule or belief; a principal is a head of a college.

items.s: Be careful not to ___ your ticket on the train.
items.h: Lose (one o) = not have any more; loose (two o's) = not tight.

items.s: My tooth is ___, so it will come out soon.
items.h: Loose (two o's) = not tight or fixed; lose = no longer have.

items.s: We bought pens, folders and other ___ for school.
items.h: Stationery (e for envelopes) = paper and pens; stationary = still.

items.s: The bus was ___ at the red traffic lights.
items.h: Stationary = not moving; stationery (e for envelopes) = pens.

items.s: She paid me a ___ on my drawing; she said it was brilliant.
items.h: A compliment (with i) is something nice that someone says to you.

items.s: This scarf is the perfect ___ to my blue coat.
items.h: A complement (with e) completes something or goes well with it.

items.s: ___ going to be a meteor shower tonight!
items.h: There's = there is; theirs = belonging to them.

items.s: ___ the girl who won the art competition?
items.h: Who's = who is; whose asks who something belongs to.

items.s: Everyone in my family ___ Sam likes spinach.
items.h: Except = apart from; accept = agree to take something.

items.s: I'm happy to ___ your kind invitation.
items.h: Accept = say yes to something offered; except = apart from.

items.s: We had ice cream for ___ after dinner.
items.h: Dessert has double s, like 'sweet stuff'; a desert is dry and sandy.

items.s: I don't know ___ it will be sunny tomorrow.
items.h: Whether means if; weather is rain, sun and snow.

items.s: Adults need a ___ to drive a car.
items.h: British English: licence (with c) is the noun; license is the verb.

items.s: We walked ___ the long tunnel to the other side.
items.h: Through = in one side and out the other; threw = past of throw.

items.s: It isn't ___ to bring a coat; it's warm outside.
items.h: Necessary has one collar and two sleeves: one c, double s.

items.s: I will ___ come to your party; I wouldn't miss it!
items.h: Definitely has finite inside it: de-finite-ly.

items.s: Please don't ___ me by showing everyone my baby photos!
items.h: Embarrass has double r and double s: em-bar-rass.

items.s: Clap your hands to the ___ of the music.
items.h: Rhythm Helps Your Two Hips Move: r-h-y-t-h-m.

items.s: My ___ told me to tell the truth.
items.h: Conscience = con + science: the voice inside that knows right.

items.s: The idea ___ to me while I was in the bath.
items.h: Occurred has double c and double r: oc-cur-red.

items.s: Please keep the glass and the plastic ___.
items.h: There's a rat in separate: sep-a-rat-e.

items.s: The shortest month of the year is ___.
items.h: Don't forget the first r: Feb-ru-ary.

items.s: I ___ a postcard from my aunt in Japan today.
items.h: I before e, except after c: received.

items.s: The ___ for the bus went all the way round the corner.
items.h: Queue: q, then u-e-u-e. Four of its five letters are vowels!

items.s: My cousin speaks three ___ languages.
items.h: Foreign breaks the i-before-e rule: f-o-r-e-i-g-n.

items.s: Our school council is a ___ of six pupils.
items.h: Committee doubles m, t and e: co-mm-i-tt-ee.

items.s: Can you ___ a good book for me to read?
items.h: Recommend = re + commend: one c, double m.

items.s: Being chosen for the team is a real ___.
items.h: Privilege has no d: p-r-i-v-i-l-e-g-e.

items.s: Regular practice will help you ___ your goals.
items.h: I before e, except after c: achieve.

items.s: The weather is ___ today: sun, then snow, then sun!
items.h: Weird is weird: it breaks the i-before-e rule.

items.s: The cat's ___ behaviour got it into lots of trouble.
items.h: Mischievous has no i after the v: mis-chie-vous.

items.s: I ___ my friend's voice at once on the phone.
items.h: Recognise has cog in the middle: re-cog-nise.

items.s: The ___ in the classroom was 22 degrees.
items.h: Say it slowly: tem-per-a-ture, with an a in the middle.

items.s: There was thunder and ___ during the storm.
items.h: Lightning, the flash in a storm, has no e: light-ning.

items.s: Wash your hands often for good ___.
items.h: Hygiene: hy-gi-ene, with i before e.

items.s: Today is my sister's ___ birthday.
items.h: Twelve becomes twelfth: keep the f sound, then add th.

items.s: We need to ___ a decision about the class trip today.
items.h: Decision goes with make: make a decision, make a choice.

items.s: Thirty schools will ___ part in the competition.
items.h: Take part = join in: thirty schools will take part.

items.s: Please ___ attention to the safety instructions.
items.h: We pay attention to something; we never make attention.

items.s: Scientists ___ research to find new medicines.
items.h: Research goes with do: do research, do homework.

items.s: Everyone ___ mistakes; that's how we learn.
items.h: Mistake goes with make: everyone makes mistakes.

items.s: Our school play will ___ place in the main hall.
items.h: Take place = happen: the play will take place in the hall.

items.s: I promise I'll ___ my best in the test.
items.h: Best goes with do: do your best.

items.s: Can I ___ a go on your scooter?
items.h: Have a go = try something: can I have a go?

items.s: Our class has ___ great progress with fractions.
items.h: Progress goes with make: we have made great progress.

items.s: You must always ___ the truth.
items.h: We tell the truth, tell a story and tell a joke.

items.s: It was ___ cold, so we wore thick gloves.
items.h: Bitterly cold is the strong way to say very cold.

items.s: We had ___ rain all night, and the river rose.
items.h: We say heavy rain, not strong rain.

items.s: The baby was ___ asleep in her cot.
items.h: Fast asleep = sleeping very deeply.

items.s: Let's ___ in touch over the summer holidays.
items.h: Keep in touch = stay in contact with someone.

items.s: We ___ an experiment to test which paper is strongest.
items.h: Carry out = do or perform: carry out an experiment.

items.s: Recycling can really ___ a difference to our planet.
items.h: Make a difference = have a good effect.

items.s: We need to ___ awareness about plastic in the ocean.
items.h: Raise awareness = help more people know about something.

items.s: Remember to ___ notes during the lesson.
items.h: Take notes = write down the important points.

items.s: Our team ___ the school record for the relay race!
items.h: Break a record = do better than anyone has before.

items.s: It's highly ___ that it will snow here in July.
items.h: Highly unlikely = almost certainly will not happen.

items.s: It all depends ___ the weather.
items.h: Depend always takes on: it depends on the weather.

items.s: The captain is responsible ___ the team's equipment.
items.h: Responsible takes for: responsible for the equipment.

items.s: This robot is capable ___ climbing stairs.
items.h: Capable takes of + -ing: capable of climbing.

items.s: Penguins are very different ___ polar bears.
items.h: Different from is the safest choice: different from polar bears.

items.s: My brother is really keen ___ astronomy.
items.h: Keen takes on: keen on astronomy.

items.s: The village is famous ___ its cheese.
items.h: Famous takes for: famous for its cheese.

items.s: Water consists ___ hydrogen and oxygen.
items.h: Consist takes of: water consists of hydrogen and oxygen.

items.s: Are you aware ___ the new school rules?
items.h: Aware takes of: are you aware of the rules?

items.s: We congratulated her ___ winning the art prize.
items.h: Congratulate someone on something: congratulated her on winning.

items.s: He apologised ___ being late.
items.h: Apologise takes for (the reason) and to (the person).

items.s: This scarf belongs ___ my grandmother.
items.h: Belong takes to: it belongs to my grandmother.

items.s: The new rules will prevent cars ___ parking outside school.
items.h: Prevent someone from doing something: prevent cars from parking.

items.s: He succeeded ___ building a working robot.
items.h: Succeed takes in + -ing: succeeded in building.

items.s: Try to concentrate ___ your work, please.
items.h: Concentrate takes on: concentrate on your work.

items.s: I deleted the photo ___ accident, not on purpose.
items.h: By accident = not on purpose.

items.s: We booked our tickets ___ advance.
items.h: In advance = before the time: book in advance.

items.s: My handwriting is very similar ___ my dad's.
items.h: Similar takes to: similar to my dad's.

items.s: I'm not very good ___ remembering names.
items.h: Good takes at: good at remembering names.

items.s: Our class took part ___ a beach clean-up.
items.h: Take part in = join an activity: took part in a clean-up.

items.s: The maths quiz was a piece of ___; I finished in minutes.
items.h: A piece of cake = very easy.

items.s: Our teacher told a joke to break the ___ on the first day.
items.h: Break the ice = help people relax and start talking.

items.s: We only eat out once in a ___ moon, so it's a treat.
items.h: Once in a blue moon = very rarely.

items.s: When I won the prize, I was over the ___!
items.h: Over the moon = extremely happy.

items.s: Please don't spill the ___ about the surprise party!
items.h: Spill the beans = tell a secret too early.

items.s: My brother let the cat out of the ___ about my present.
items.h: Let the cat out of the bag = give away a secret by mistake.

items.s: The new bike cost an arm and a ___!
items.h: Cost an arm and a leg = be very expensive.

items.s: You hit the nail on the ___; that's exactly right!
items.h: Hit the nail on the head = say exactly the right thing.

items.s: I've done my part; now the ball is in your ___.
items.h: The ball is in your court = it's your turn to decide or act.

items.s: I had butterflies in my ___ before the school play.
items.h: Butterflies in your stomach = feeling nervous.

items.s: We lost the instructions, so it's back to square ___.
items.h: Back to square one = back to the very start.

items.s: We built the go-kart from ___, with no kit at all.
items.h: From scratch = from the very beginning, with nothing ready-made.

items.s: Hold your ___! Wait until everyone is ready.
items.h: Hold your horses = wait, don't rush.

items.s: I'm all ___; tell me about your holiday!
items.h: I'm all ears = I'm listening carefully.

items.s: The litter on the beach is only the tip of the ___.
items.h: The tip of the iceberg = a small part of a much bigger problem.

items.s: Learning to code isn't rocket ___; anyone can do it!
items.h: It's not rocket science = it isn't very difficult.

items.s: Don't sit on the ___; tell us which team you support!
items.h: Sit on the fence = avoid choosing a side.

items.s: All that fuss over a lost pen was a storm in a ___.
items.h: A storm in a teacup = a big fuss about something small.

items.s: On my first day in the band, I had to learn the ___.
items.h: Learn the ropes = learn how to do something new.
